lastMessage:
I couldn't run the tests, so what follows comes from reading the code, not from a test run.

**Why it didn't run:** the sandbox is read-only for the project directory, `$HOME` and `$TMPDIR`. GUT needs `godot --headless --import` first, to write `.godot/` and its class-name cache. That write fails with `Read-only file system`, and `gut_cmdln.gd` then aborts with "Some GUT class_names have not been imported". I didn't try to get around the sandbox. If you allow writes to the project directory, or run the import yourself, I can do the real run.

**Test that fails, by my reading:** `test_every_fifth_hit_raises_the_multiplier` at `test/test_score.gd:7`: `assert_eq(score.hit(10), 25)`.
- **Expected:** 25.
- **Got:** 20. On the 5th hit `combo` is 5, so `score.gd` computes `10 * (1 + 5/5)`, which is `10 * 2`, giving 20. The integer division `combo / 5` gives a whole-number multiplier.
- **Who is wrong:** most likely the test. A whole-number multiplier on a hit worth 10 can only give 10, 20, 30 and so on, so 25 would need a 2.5× multiplier. The game code matches its own description of "every fifth hit raises the multiplier". I can't be certain, though, because no spec says what the intended number is. If 2.5× was intended, the game would be the one at fault.

The other two tests (`test_miss_resets_combo` and `test_main_scene_scores_on_ready`) look like they pass. Combo goes to 0 after a miss, and `main.gd` makes 12 hits in `_ready`, so `points` is above 0.

I haven't edited any files.

input.command: ls addons addons/*; cat test/test_score.gd score.gd

export XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/claude-eval-LrbWh5/home/xdg; mkdir -p $XDG_DATA_HOME; "$EVAL_GODOT_BIN" --headless --import 2>&1 | tail -5; "$EVAL_GODOT_BIN" --headless -s addons/gut/gut_cmdln.gd -gdir=res://test -gexit 2>&1 | tail -40; git status --short
pwd; touch ./x_probe && echo cwd-ok && rm x_probe; ls -d .godot 2>&1; echo $TMPDIR $HOME
